label: sparse: copy-phase input v before output m, or step 3-4 after m/g prefix
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.012% of steps). It has two loose tendencies. (1) Copy phase (63% of mass): the fed-back input is v (16.9x lift, about half of activations), often when the next output is m or w. (2) Original phase at t=3-4 (37% of mass): the prefix contains g, frequently starting m g g; the strongest activations are m g g [x] at t=3. Neither tendency is selective. Copy-phase v fires on only 0.4% of its occurrences, and adding out_tok==m raises that to just 6%. The exact m g g prefix at t=3 reaches 65% precision but covers only 3% of activations. It never fires at t<3, at the delimiter, or once copying has gone wrong. No simple token or position predicate gets above about 0.12 F1, so activation probably depends on a specific hidden-state configuration that these variables do not capture.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=v (+4.17), phase=2 & out_tok=m (+3.55), prev_tok=g (+3.32), t=3 & prev_tok=g (+2.96), phase=2 & out_tok=w (+2.93), prev_tok=e (+2.67). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-2.05), t=10 (-1.47), t=11 (-1.40).
